Interviewer: Molly Murphy with recording engineer Ken Kimery Institution Description: Transcript, 23 pp.
Molly Murphy: Okay, I’d like to begin by just setting the scene here. It is January 10th, 2010.
The microphone is now on so that’s helpful. Mr. Wess, you were born in 1922 so you are currently 88. Is that right? Okay, and you just so we have this down, you were named an NEA Jazz Master in 2007.

So, today we are going to, as I just mentioned, we are going to pick up from where you may have left off in your original Smithsonian oral history interview. Ken Kimery: Let me interrupt for just a second there, the levels are just a little bit low. Sorry about that.

Anyway, we are picking up from where you may have left off six or seven years ago when your oral history was done in 2003 by Bill Brauer. So, to begin, we just had Dr. Billy Taylor in the room; I don’t know if you ran into each other in the lobby there.
(Laughs) That’s too bad; he was hoping that he would run into you. Anyways, he and I were remembering when you and I went up to his place. It was probably about 2000
